questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a university that had a broad range of studies that would support my degree and give me a better perspective and wider view on cultures and practice of my field internationally, and that would also give me new opportunities that my home university maybe couldn't.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was especially interesting to learn the focus points of the same degree in a different culture and how they choose to teach the different topics.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Macquarie University had sent a good and thorough e-mail explaining the whole process and good tips on getting there, places to live, the costs of living and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was orientation days with people showing us around campus, giving us tips and offer lectures on how to use the different online websites and so on. There was a lot of help, to guide us, you just had to actively participate and say yes to the help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing via. website that the university had suggested - which helped. Unfortunately the housing provided by the university was very, very expensive and also almost completely booked very early on in the process.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Be careful with who you choose as your landlord and roommates, it doesn't come without risk unfortunately. Always meet the people first, and see the place before you agree to move in and make sure to have a contract from the first day, so you're sure to get your deposit back. 
Other than that, living off campus can give great opportunities to see different sides of the country, meet other people and maybe get a more clear and authentic experience of how it is to live in that culture. I would definitely recommend it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is overall very expensive, the housing available to students from the university was generally more expensuve than what you could find off campus - which doesn't really makes sense to me. Most housing opportunities are share-houses.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot to go through, and the process + website was very confusing - especially the process of signing up for classes and getting them approved.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There's almost too much to remember... First the application, which was fine, then paying the health care cover and sending the proof, then the approval letter and getting an email, checking classes, signing up for classes - getting them approved there - and also at my home university, then figuring out the different student websites (I think 3 overall...) and checking that the schedules of your approved classes doesn't collide and so on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the university staff that was in charge of exchange or try and find the answer on the websites, but mostly I found help from my friends that I had met at the University and already knew the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to try a few rounds before I found classes that didn't collide with each other and that was provided for the semester I was attending (the summer semester) and not the winter semester. Initially I was mostky interested in the classes provided for the winter semester, but I did love most of the classes I got.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a great campus and school, make sure to check the available classes first and see how many interest you and if the match your degree and are able to teach you something that your home university might not. If you are ever in doubt about something, reach out to the fellow students of the university, they give quick answers and are happy to help. I would also recommend signing up for some of the student groups/activities they provide, it is a great way to explore, and meet other people. And be sure to make it to the orientation week! It'll help a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 4 courses, each 10 points, they had a bigger focus on weekly tasks and practical learning, than my home university that focuses more on reading and exams. It was a nice switch up - but a mix of both would have been ideal for learning outcome.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical approach, less reading, more small written task, less bigger written papers and exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Radio and podcast production
Media and communications: Creative  contexts
Performance practices
Non-fiction screen media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Performance practices were amazing and so fun! You learn in e very practical and good way.
Radio and podcast production is also higly recommended at it was also very fun and I learned a lot of creative tools that I can use in various ways.
Both classes had great teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The health insurance only covers a very little part of the doctors appointments - even just the consultation. Be very sure when going to the doctors, and have a danish travel insurance that can probably cover the rest that the OSHC doesn't cover.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and rent were more expensive than expected...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a lot of different clubs and activities you could attend! most of them might cost money though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, everyone of them is listed on their website, so you can check them in advance, and they all have booths at orientation week, so you can go and check them out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is the exchange student club which was good and created great opportunities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel a bit, if you have the time/ money - maybe not to the more exploited places of australia, but just an hour or two away from the town you're staying at and explore the small places and see the "real life".

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy - but I am also an extrovert...

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for the different student clubs that interest you, try and live with new people - so not people you know from home or with more than just them and reach out to people from your home country that are going to the same host country/ university, so you don't feel completely alone when you arrive and can rely on them for support when in doubt or confused about the process. And go to the intro week!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The culture here was a lot different than what I imagined about Australie, there is a huge asian influence now which is amazing and really creates a cool perspective!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a hostel for the first few days while you visit places you might rent, if you're not staying with the university accommodation. Don't have flight ticket home already - you might want to alter your stay. Have money saved up sp you can go on adventures and try and find a casual job as well, so you don*t have to worry too much about money + it'll give you a better insight on life here and create more friend opportunities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just choose your classes carefully and remember to have fun!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I got here! Through University, Living situations and work!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a good place to live (I was unfortunate with landlords and roommates and had to move around 3 times) And also just affording to live while inflation is going on...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
